1	\section{Types}
     2	\label{sec:types}
     3	
     4	We augment the definition of conditionally linear functions with a construct
     5	we call \emph{types}.
     6	A type~$\tvar$ is an element of a \emph{type set} $\type$, and a $\type$-typed
     7	family of conditionally linear functions is a collection
     8	$\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar\in\type}$ containing a CL function $L_\tvar$ for each
     9	type~$\tvar\in\type$.
    10	The utility of this definition is that it allows us to define another object,
    11	namely conditionally linear distributions parameterized by an undirected graph
    12	$G = (\type, E)$ on the set of types known as a \emph{type graph}.
    13	Given two $\type$-typed families of conditionally linear functions
    14	$\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type}, \{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$, the $(\type,
    15	G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution corresponding to them is the
    16	distribution which samples a pair of types $(\lvar, \rvar)$ uniformly at random
    17	from the edges of~$G$ (with each endpoint having equal probability as being
    18	chosen for $\lvar$ or $\rvar$, respectively) and then samples $(x, y)$ from
    19	$\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    20	The output is the pair $( (\lvar, x), (\rvar, y) )$.
    21	
    22	The normal form verifiers we present in the paper frequently use typed CL
    23	distributions to sample their questions, rather than untyped CL distributions.
    24	Types allow us to model the parts of their question distributions which are
    25	unstructured and unsuitable for being sampled from CL distributions.
    26	A common use of types is to allow the verifier to use previously defined games
    27	as subroutines.
    28	Here, the type helps indicate which subroutine the verifier selects, and an edge
    29	in the type graph between two different types allows us to introduce a test that
    30	cross-checks the results of one subroutine with the results of another.
    31	
    32	Finally, we show how to convert any typed CL distribution into an equivalent (in
    33	the precise sense defined below) untyped CL distribution with two additional
    34	levels, a technique we call \emph{detyping}.
    35	This entails showing how to ``simulate'' the \emph{graph distribution} of $G =
    36	(\type, E)$, i.e.\ the uniform distribution on its edges, using an untyped CL
    37	distribution.
    38	The simulation we give is based on rejection sampling and is only approximate:
    39	its quality degrades exponentially with the number of types in~$\type$.
    40	As a result, we will ensure throughout the paper that all type sets we consider
    41	are of a small, in fact generally constant, size.
    42	
    43	This section is organized as follows.
    44	In \cref{sec:typed-samplers} we define typed variants of CL distributions,
    45	samplers, deciders, and verifiers.
    46	In \cref{sec:graph-dist} we define a CL distribution which samples from the
    47	graph distribution of a given graph $G = (\type, E)$.
    48	In \cref{sec:detype} we define a canonical way to detype typed samplers,
    49	deciders, and verifiers using the graph sampler from \cref{sec:graph-dist}.
    50	We then prove the main result of the section, \cref{lem:detyping-verifiers},
    51	which relates the value of the detyped normal form verifier to the value of
    52	the original typed verifier.
    53	
    54	\subsection{Typed samplers, deciders, and verifiers}
    55	\label{sec:typed-samplers}
    56	
    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}
    94	
    95	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear samplers]
    96	  \label{def:typed-sampler}
    97		Let $q:\N \to \N$ be an admissible field size function and $s: \N \to \N$ be a
    98	  function.
    99	  Let $\type$ be a finite type set and let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
   100	  A $7$-input Turing machine $\sampler$ is a \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed, $\ell$-level
   101	    conditionally linear sampler with field size $q(n)$ and dimension $s(n)$} if
   102	  for all $n \in \N$, letting $q = q(n)$ and $s = s(n)$, there exist
   103	  $\type$-typed families of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   104	  $\{L^{\alice,\, n}_{\tvar}\}_{\tvar \in \type}$ and $\{L^{\bob,\,
   105	    n}_{\tvar}\}_{\tvar \in \type}$ on $V = \F_q^s$ where $\tvar \in \type, w\in
   106	  \AB$, the conditionally linear function $L^{w,\, n}_{\tvar}$ has marginal
   107	  functions $\{L^{w,\, n}_{\tvar,\, \leq j}\}$ and factor spaces $\{V^{w,\,
   108	    n}_{\tvar,\, j,\, u}\}$ satisfying the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-kth},
   109	  and for all $\tvar \in \type$, $w \in \ab$, $j \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$, and
   110	  $z \in V$:
   111	  \begin{itemize}
   112	  \item On input $(n, \gamestyle{dimension})$, the sampler $\sampler$ returns
   113	    the dimension $s(n)$.
   114		
   115		\item On input $(n, w, \gamestyle{marginal}, j, z, \tvar)$, the sampler
   116	    $\sampler$ returns the binary representation of $L^{w,\, n}_{\tvar,\, \le
   117	      j}(z)$.
   118				
   119				\item On input $(n, w, \gamestyle{linear}, j, u, y, \tvar)$, the sampler $\sampler$
   120	    outputs the binary representation of $L^{w,\, n}_{\tvar,\, j,\, u}(y)$,
   121	
   122		\item On input $(n, w, \gamestyle{factor}, j, u, \tvar)$, the sampler
   123	    $\sampler$ returns the factor space $V^{w,\, n}_{\tvar,\, j,\, u}$ of
   124	    $L^{w,\, n}_{\tvar}$, represented as an indicator vector in $\{0,1\}^s$.
   125	  \end{itemize}
   126	  We call $\F_{q(n)}^{s(n)}$ the \emph{ambient space of $\sampler$}.
   127	  We call $\{ L^{\alice,\, n}_{\tvar} \}, \{ L^{\bob,\, n}_{\tvar} \}$ the
   128	  \emph{CL functions of $\sampler$ on index $n$}.
   129	  The \emph{time complexity} of $\sampler$, denoted $\TIME_\sampler(n)$, is the
   130	  number of steps before $\sampler$ halts for index $n$.
   131	\end{definition}
   132	
   133	We assume that types $\tvar \in \type$ are represented using binary strings of
   134	length at most $\lceil \log |\type| \rceil$; if a type $\tvar$ is given as input
   135	to the sampler $\sampler$ and is not an element of $\type$, then the sampler
   136	returns $0$.
   137	Furthermore, as described in Remark~\ref{rmk:sampler-inputs} for un-typed
   138	samplers, we write typed samplers with different numbers of arguments depending
   139	on the input.
   140	We note that Definition~\ref{def:typed-sampler} includes the graph $G$ as a parameter, even though it is not explicitly used anywhere;
   141	this is so we can define the following concept, i.e.\ the \emph{distribution} of a typed sampler, which \emph{does} depend on $G$.
   142	
   143	\begin{definition}[Distribution of a typed sampler]
   144	  \label{def:typed-sampler-sample}
   145	  Let $\sampler$ be a $(\type, G)$-typed sampler.
   146	  Let $L^w = \{ L^{w}_{\tvar} \}_\tvar$ for $w\in \{\alice, \bob\}$ be the CL
   147	  functions of $\sampler$ on index~$n$.
   148	  The \emph{distribution of sampler $\sampler$ on index $n$},
   149	  denoted $\mu^G_{\sampler,\, n}$, is the $(\type, G)$-typed conditionally
   150	  linear distribution corresponding to $(L^\alice, L^\bob)$.
   151	\end{definition}
   152	
   153	\begin{definition}[Downsizing typed CL samplers]
   154	  \label{def:downsize-typed-sampler}
   155	Let $\sampler$ be a typed sampler.
   156	  The typed downsized sampler $\downsize(\sampler)$ is defined as in
   157	  Definition~\ref{def:downsize_sampler} with the only difference that the type
   158	  $\tvar$ is included as part of the input to the sampler, as in
   159	  Definition~\ref{def:typed-sampler}.
   160	\end{definition}
   161	
   162	\begin{lemma}
   163	  \label{lem:downsize_typed_sampler}
   164	Let $\sampler$ be a $(\type, G)$-typed $\ell$-level CL sampler, for some finite set
   165	  $\type$, graph $G$,  and integer $\ell\geq 0$.
   166	  Let $q(n)$ and $s(n)$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:typed-sampler}.
   167	  Then $\downsize(\sampler)$ defined in
   168	  Definition~\ref{def:downsize-typed-sampler} is a $(\type, G)$-typed $\ell$-level CL
   169	  sampler with field size $2$, dimension $s(n) \log q(n)$, and
   170	  time complexity
   171	  \begin{equation*}
   172	    \TIME_{\downsize(\sampler)}(n) = O(\TIME_\sampler(n) \log q(n))\;.
   173	  \end{equation*}
   174	  Furthermore, for every integer $n \geq 1$, the CL functions of
   175	  $\downsize(\sampler)$ on index $n$ are
   176	  $\{(L_\tvar^{w,n})^\downsize\}_{w\in\{\alice,\bob\}, \tvar\in\type}$, as
   177	  defined in Definition~\ref{def:cl-downsize}.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181	  The proof is analogous to the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_sampler}, and
   182	  we omit it.
   183	\end{proof}
   184	
   185	\begin{definition}[Typed decider]
   186	  \label{def:typed-decider}
   187	  A \emph{typed decider} is a $7$-input Turing machine $\decider$ that on all
   188	  inputs of the form $(n,\lvar,x,\rvar,y,a,b)$ where $n$ is an integer and
   189	  $\lvar,x,\rvar,y,a,b \in \{0,1\}^*$, $\decider$ halts and returns a single
   190	  bit.
   191	  When $\decider$ returns $0$ we say that it \emph{rejects}, otherwise we say
   192	  that it \emph{accepts}.
   193	  We use $\TIME_\decider(n)$ to denote the time complexity of $\decider$ on
   194	  inputs of the form $(n,\ldots)$.
   195	\end{definition}
   196	
   197	\begin{definition}
   198	  \label{def:typed-normal-ver}
   199	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph.
   200	  A $(\type, G)$-\emph{typed normal form verifier} is a pair $\verifier =
   201	  (\sampler, \decider)$ where $\sampler$ is a $(\type,G)$-typed sampler with field
   202	  size $q(n) = 2$ and $\decider$ is a typed decider.
   203	\end{definition}
   204	
   205	\begin{definition}
   206	  \label{def:typed-normal-game}
   207	  Let $\verifier = (\sampler, \decider)$ be a $(\type, G)$-typed normal form
   208	  verifier.
   209	  For $n \in \N$, we define the following nonlocal game $\verifier_{n}$ to be
   210	  the \emph{$n$-th game corresponding to the verifier $\verifier$}.
   211	  The question sets $\cal{X}$ and $\cal{Y}$ are $\type \times
   212	  \{0,1\}^{\TIME_\sampler(n)}$.
   213	  The answer sets $\cal{A}$ and $\cal{B}$ are $\{0,1\}^{\TIME_\decider(n)}$.
   214	  The question distribution is the distribution $\mu^G_{\sampler,\, n}$
   215	  specified in Definition~\ref{def:typed-sampler-sample}.
   216	  The decision predicate is the function computed by
   217	  $\decider(n,\lvar,x,\rvar,y,a,b)$, when the inputs $((\lvar, x), (\rvar, y), a, b)$ are
   218	  restricted to $\cal{X}\times \cal{Y}\times\cal{A}\times\cal{B}$.
   219	  The value of the game is denoted by $\val^*(\verifier_{n})$.  
   220	\end{definition}
   221	
   222	For $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$ and a question $(\lvar, x)$ to player $w$ we refer to
   223	$\lvar$ as the \emph{question type} and $x$ as the \emph{question content}.
   224	
   225	\subsection{Graph distributions}
   226	\label{sec:graph-dist}
   227	
   228	We describe a construction of conditionally linear distributions which sample
   229	from the graph distribution (see Definition~\ref{def:graph-distribution}) of a
   230	graph $G = (U, E)$.
   231	We begin with a technical definition, followed by the definition of the
   232	conditionally linear distribution.
   233	
   234	\begin{definition}[Neighbor indicator]\label{def:type-neighbor}
   235	  Given a graph $G = (U, E)$, the \emph{neighbor indicator} of a vertex $u \in
   236	  U$ is the vector $\mathrm{neigh}_G(u) \in \F_2^U$ in which, for all $v \in U$,
   237	  \begin{equation*}
   238	    \mathrm{neigh}_G(u)_v =
   239	    \begin{cases}
   240	      1 & \text{ if } \{u, v\} \in E,\\
   241	      0 & \text{ otherwise}.
   242	    \end{cases}
   243	  \end{equation*}
   244	  In addition, the \emph{$\F_2$-encoding} of a vertex $u \in U$ is the vector
   245	  $\mathrm{enc}_G(u) \in \F_2^U \times \F_2^U$ given by $\mathrm{enc}_G(u) =
   246	  (e_u, \mathrm{neigh}_G(u))$, where $e_u$ is the standard basis vector with
   247	  a~$1$ in the $u$-th position and $0$'s everywhere else.
   248	\end{definition}
   249	
   250	\begin{definition}[Graph sampler]\label{def:graph-sampler}
   251	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be a graph with $n$ vertices.
   252	  Then the \emph{conditionally linear functions corresponding to~$G$} are the
   253	  pair of functions $L_G^\alice, L_G^\bob$ on linear space $V_G$ specified in
   254	  \cref{fig:graph-distribution} where $V_G = V_{\vertex{\alice}} \oplus
   255	  V_{\edge{\alice}} \oplus V_{\vertex{\bob}} \oplus V_{\edge{\bob}}$.
   256	\end{definition}

1	\section{Nonlocal Games and $\MIP^*$}
     2	\label{sec:games}
     3	
     4	We introduce definitions associated with nonlocal games and strategies that will
     5	be used throughout.
     6	
     7	\subsection{Games and strategies}
     8	\label{sec:strat}
     9	
    10	\begin{definition}[Two-player one-round games]
    11	  \label{def:game}
    12	  A \emph{two-player one-round game} $\game$ is specified by a tuple
    13	  $(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ where
    14	  \begin{enumerate}
    15	  \item $\cal{X}$ and $\cal{Y}$ are finite sets (called the \emph{question
    16	      alphabets}),
    17	  \item $\cal{A}$ and $\cal{B}$ are finite sets (called the \emph{answer
    18	      alphabets}),
    19	  \item $\mu$ is a probability distribution over $\cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$
    20	    (called the \emph{question distribution}), and
    21	  \item $D: \cal{X} \times \cal{Y} \times \cal{A} \times \cal{B} \to \{0,1\}$ is
    22	    a function (called the \emph{decision predicate}).
    23	  \end{enumerate}
    24	\end{definition}
    25	
    26	\begin{definition}[Tensor product strategies]
    27	  \label{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    28	  A \emph{tensor product strategy} $\strategy$ for a game $\game = (\cal{X},
    29	  \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is a tuple $(\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ where
    30	  \begin{itemize}
    31		\item $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure quantum state, i.e.\ a unit vector in $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ for finite
    32	    dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mH_A, \mH_B$,
    33		\item $A$ is a set $\{A^x\}$ such that for every $x \in \cal{X}$, $A^x =
    34	    \{A^x_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_A$, and
    35		\item $B$ is a set $\{B^y\}$ such that for every $y \in \cal{Y}$, $B^y =
    36	    \{B^y_b \}_{b \in \cal{B}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_B$.
    37	\end{itemize}
    38	\end{definition}
    39	
    40	\begin{definition}[Tensor product value]
    41	  \label{def:tensor-product-value}
    42		The \emph{tensor product value} of a tensor product strategy $\strategy =
    43	  (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$  with respect to a game $\game=(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A},
    44	  \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is defined as
    45	  \begin{equation*}
    46			\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \sum_{x,\, y,\, a,\, b} \, \mu(x,y)\, D(x,y,a,b)\,
    47	    \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^y_b\, \ket{\psi}\;.
    48	  \end{equation*}
    49		For $v\in[0,1]$ we say that the strategy $\strategy$ \emph{passes (or wins)
    50	    $\game$ with probability $v$ if} $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \geq v$.
    51	  The \emph{tensor product value} of $\game$ is defined as
    52	  \begin{equation*}
    53			\val^*(\game) = \sup_\strategy \val^*(\game, \strategy)\;,
    54	  \end{equation*}
    55		where the supremum is taken over all tensor product strategies $\strategy$ for
    56	  $\game$.
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	
    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}
    66	
    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}
   181	
   182	
   183	Recall that for a (pure) state $\ket{\psi}\in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$, the \emph{Schmidt rank} of $\ket{\psi}$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that 
   184	\[ \ket{\psi} = \sum_{i=1}^k\, \alpha_i \ket{u_i}\otimes \ket{v_i}\;,\]
   185	for some orthonormal families $\{\ket{u_i}\}\subset \mH_\alice$ and $\{\ket{v_i}\}\subset\mH_\bob$ and $\alpha_i>0$. The coefficients $\alpha_i$ are uniquely defined by $\ket{\psi}$ and called \emph{Schmidt coefficients}. The state $\ket{\psi}$ is called \emph{maximally entangled} if $\alpha_i=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots,k$.  
   186	
   187	
   188	\begin{definition}[Entanglement requirements of a game]
   189	  \label{def:ent}
   190		For all games $\game$ and $\nu \in [0, 1]$, let $\Ent(\game, \nu)$ denote the
   191	  minimum integer $d$ such that there exists a finite dimensional tensor product
   192	  strategy $\strategy$ that achieves success probability at least $\nu$ in the
   193	  game $\game$ with a state $\ket{\psi}$ whose Schmidt rank is at most $d$.
   194	  If there is no finite dimensional strategy that achieves success probability
   195	  $\nu$, then define $\Ent(\game, \nu)$ to be $\infty$.
   196	\end{definition}
   197	
   198	
   199	
   200	\begin{remark}
   201	  A strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for a symmetric game $\game =
   202	  (\cal{X}, \cal{X}, \cal{A}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ is called \emph{synchronous} if
   203	  it holds that for every $x\in \cal{X}$ and $a\neq b \in \cal{A}$, $\bra{\psi}
   204	  A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi} = 0$; in other words,
   205	  the players never return different answers when simultaneously asked the same
   206	  question.
   207	  As shown in~\cite{paulsen2016estimating} the condition for a
   208	  finite-dimensional strategy of being synchronous is equivalent to the
   209	  condition that it is projective, consistent, and moreover $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   210	  maximally entangled state.
   211	  (The equivalence is extended to infinite-dimensional strategies, as well as
   212	  correlations induced by limits of finite-dimensional strategies,
   213	  in~\cite{kim2018synchronous}.)
   214	\end{remark}
   215	\subsection{Distance measures}
   216	
   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.
   218	
   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.
   224	  For some function $\delta : \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{ \ket{\psi_n} \}$ and
   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}
   226	  \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if $ \norm{\ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n}}^2 =
   227	  O(\delta(n))$.
   228	  (For convenience we generally leave the dependence of the states and $\delta$
   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)
   230	\end{definition}
   231	
   232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for
   236	  all $x\in \mX$, $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ POVMs.
   237	  We write
   238	  \begin{equation*}
   239	    A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a
   240	  \end{equation*}
   241	  on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_{a\ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi}
   244	    = O(\delta)\;.\footnote{Here the use of the $O(\cdot)$ notation refers to the fact that the notation will often be used to measure consistency for \emph{famillies} of POVM and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n\in \mathbb{N}$, which will always be clear from context but omitted for legibility, see Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}. The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}
   245	  \end{equation*}
   246	  In this case, we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are
   247	  \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$.
   248	\end{definition}
   249	
   250	Note that a consistent measurement on $\ket{\psi}$ according to
   251	Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same $\ket{\psi}$ and under
   252	the singleton distribution, according to Definition~\ref{def:consistency} (and
   253	vice-versa). This is because 
   254	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} =1 \,\implies \, \forall a\;,\;\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi} = M_a \otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\;,\]
   255	because using that $\{M_a\}$ is a POVM there must be equality in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
   256	\[ 1 = \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\, \leq\, \Big(\sum_a \|\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)\Big(\sum_a \|M_a\otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)^{1/2} \,\leq\,1 \;.\]
   257	
   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}
   268	  and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state
   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.
   271	\end{definition}
   272	
   273	\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]
   274	  \label{def:strategy-distance}
   275	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game
   276	  and let $\strategy = (\psi, A, B)$, $\strategy' = (\psi', A', B')$ be 
   277	  strategies for $\game$.
   278	  For $\delta\in[0,1]$ we say that \emph{$\strategy$ is $\delta$-close to
   279	    $\strategy'$} if the following conditions hold.
   280	  \begin{enumerate}
   281		\item The states $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\psi'}$ are states in the same
   282	    Hilbert space $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ and are $\delta$-close.
   283		\item For all $x \in \cal{X}, y \in \cal{Y}$, we have $A^x_a \approx_\delta
   284	    (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \approx_\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations
   285	    holding under the distribution $\mu$, and on either $\ket{\psi}$ or
   286	    $\ket{\psi'}$.
   287	  \end{enumerate}
   288	\end{definition}
   289	
   290	We record several useful facts about the consistency measure and the
   291	state-dependent distance without proof.
   292	Readers are referred to Sections 4.4 and 4.5 in~\cite{NW19} for additional
   293	discussion and proofs.
   294	
   295	\begin{fact}[Fact 4.13 and Fact 4.14 in~\cite{NW19}]
   296	  \label{fact:agreement}
   297	  For POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$, the following hold.
   298	  \begin{enumerate}
   299	  \item If $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$ then
   300	    $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \approx_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$.
   301	    \label{item:consistency-implies-approx}
   302	  \item If $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \approx_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$
   303	    \emph{and} $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are projective measurements, then
   304	    $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$.
   305	    \label{item:both-projectors-implies-consistency}
   306	  \item If $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \approx_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$ and
   307	    either $\{A^x_a\}$ or $\{B^x_a\}$ is a projective measurement, then
   308	    $A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_{\delta^{1/2}} I_\alice \otimes B^x_a$.
   309	    \label{item:one-projector-implies-consistency}
   310	  \end{enumerate}
   311	\end{fact}

   313	\begin{fact}[Fact 4.20 in~\cite{NW19}]
   314	  \label{fact:add-a-proj}
   315	  Let $\cal{A},\cal{B},\cal{C}$ be finite sets, and let $\mu$ be a distribution
   316	  over question pairs $(x,y)$.
   317	  Let $\{A_{a,b}^x\}$ and $\{B_{a,b}^x\}$ be operators whose outcomes range over the
   318	  product set $\cal{A} \times \cal{B}$.
   319	  Suppose a set of operators $\{C_{a,c}^y\}$, whose outcomes range over the
   320	  product set $\cal{A} \times \cal{C}$, satisfies the condition $\sum_{c}
   321	  (C_{a,c}^y)^\dagger C_{a,c}^y \leq \Id$ for all $a$ and all $y$.
   322	  If $A_{a,b}^x \approx_\delta B_{a,b}^x$ on average over $x$ sampled from the
   323	  corresponding marginal of distribution $\mu$, then $C^y_{a,c} A^x_{a,b}
   324	  \approx_\delta C^y_{a,c} B^x_{a,b}$ on average over $(x,y)$ sampled from $\mu$.
   325	\end{fact}
   326	\begin{proof}
   327	  Fix questions $x,y$ and answers $a \in \cal{A},b \in \cal{B}$. We have then that
   328	  \begin{align}
   329	    \sum_{c} \left \| (C^y_{a,c} A^x_{a,b} - C^y_{a,c} B^x_{a,b} ) \ket{\psi} \right \|^2
   330	    & = \sum_{c} \bra{\psi} (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})^\dagger (C^y_{a,c})^\dagger (C^y_{a,c})
   331	      (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b} ) \ket{\psi}\\
   332	    & \leq \bra{\psi} (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})^\dagger
   333	      (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b} ) \ket{\psi} \\
   334	    & = \left \| (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})\ket{\psi} \right \|^2
   335	  \end{align}
   336	  where the inequality follows from the assumption that $\sum_c (C_{a,c}^y)^\dagger
   337	  C_{a,c}^y \leq \Id$.
   338	  Thus we obtain the desired conclusion
   339	  \begin{equation*}
   340	    \E_{(x,y) \sim \mu} \sum_{a,b,c} \left \| (C^y_{a,c} A^x_{a,b} - C^y_{a,c} B^x_{a,b} )
   341	      \ket{\psi} \right \|^2 	\leq \E_{(x,y) \sim \mu} \sum_{a,b}
   342	    \left \| (A^x_{a,b} - B^x_{a,b})\ket{\psi} \right \|^2 \leq \delta.
   343	  \end{equation*}
   344	\end{proof}
   345	
   346	
   347	\begin{fact}
   348	\label{fact:add-a-proj2}
   349	Let $\mathcal{X},\mathcal{A}$ denote finite sets, and let $\mathcal{G}$ denote a set of functions $g: \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{A}$. Let $\{A^x_a \}$, $\{B^x_a\}$ be POVMs indexed by $\mathcal{X}$ and outcomes in $\mathcal{A}$. Let $\{ S_g^x \}_{x\in \mathcal{X}, g\in\mathcal{G}}$ denote a set of operators such that for all $x \in \mathcal{X}$, $\sum_g (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \leq \Id$. 
   350	If $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$ on average over $x$, then $S_g^x A^x_{g(x)} \approx_\delta S_g^x B^x_{g(x)}$. 
   351	\end{fact}
   352	\begin{proof}
   353		We expand:
   354		\begin{align*}
   355			\E_x \sum_g \norm{ S^x_g (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)}) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \sum_g \bra{\psi} (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)})^\dagger  (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x (A^x_{g(x)} - B^x_{g(x)}) \ket{\psi} \\
   356			&= \E_x \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger  \Big(\sum_{g: g(x) = a} (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \Big) (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   357			&\leq \E_x \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   358			&= \E_x \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2.
   359		\end{align*}
   360		The inequality follows from the fact that $\sum_{g: g(x) = a} (S_g^x)^\dagger S_g^x \leq \sum_g (S_g^x)^\dagger (S_g^x) \leq \Id$. The last line is at most $\delta$ by assumption, and we obtain the desired conclusion.
   361	\end{proof}

   364	\begin{lemma}
   365	\label{lem:cool-closeness-fact}
   366	Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{A}$ be finite sets and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. Let $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a projective measurement and let $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a set of matrices. If $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$, then for all subsets $S \subseteq \mathcal{A}$, we have
   367	\[
   368		\sum_{a \in S} A^x_a \approx_\delta \sum_{a \in S} A^x_a \cdot B^x_a.
   369	\]
   370	\end{lemma}
   371	\begin{proof}
   372	We expand:
   373	\begin{align*}
   374		\E_x \norm{ \sum_{a \in S} \Big(A^x_a - A^x_a \cdot B^x_a\Big) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \norm{ \sum_{a \in S} A^x_a \cdot \Big(A^x_a - B^x_a\Big) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   375		&= \E_x \sum_{a \in S} \bra{\psi} (A^x_a - B^x_a)^\dagger A^x_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi} \\
   376		&\leq \E_x \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a -  B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2\;,
   377	\end{align*}
   378	where all expectations are taken according to $\mu$. 
   379	In the second line we used the projectivity of $\{ A^x_a \}$, and in the third line we used that $A^x_a \leq \Id$.
   380	\end{proof}

   383	\begin{fact}[Triangle inequality, Fact 4.28 in~\cite{NW19}]
   384	  \label{fact:triangle}
   385	  If $A_a^x \approx_\delta B_a^x$ and $B_a^x \approx_\epsilon C_a^x$, then
   386	  $A_a^x \approx_{\delta + \epsilon} C_a^x$.

   390	 \label{fact:triangle-for-simeq}

   392	 $C_a^x \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes  B_a^x$,
   393	 and $C_a^x \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\gamma I_\alice \otimes  D_a^x$,

   404	The state-dependent distance is the right tool for reasoning about the closeness
   405	of measurement operators in a strategy.
   406	The following lemma ensures that, when two families of measurements are close on a
   407	state, changing from one family of measurement to the other only introduces
   408	a small error to the value of the strategy.
   409	
   410	\begin{lemma}
   411	  \label{lem:commutation-analysis}
   412	  Let $\{A^x_{a,\, b}\}$, $\{B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\}$, $\{C^x_{a,\, c}\}$ be POVMs.
   413	  Suppose $\{B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\}$ is projective, and
   414	  \begin{align*}
   415	    A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes \Id_\bob &\approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b}\;,\\
   416	    C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob &\approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}\;,
   417	  \end{align*}
   418		where recall that $B^x_{a,\, b} = \sum_c B^x_{a,b,c}$ and similarly $B^x_{a,\, c}=\sum_b B^x_{a,b,c}$. 
   419	  Then the following approximate commutation relation holds:
   420	  \begin{equation*}
   421	    [A^x_{a,\, b}, C^x_{a,\, c}] \otimes I_\bob \approx_\delta 0\;.
   422	  \end{equation*}
   423	\end{lemma}
   424	
   425	\begin{proof}
   426	  Applying Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to $C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob
   427	  \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}$ and $\{A^x_{a,b} \otimes
   428	  \Id_\bob \}$, we have
   429	  \begin{equation}
   430	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-1}
   431	    A^x_{a,\, b} C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob
   432	    \approx_\delta A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}\,.
   433	  \end{equation}
   434	  Similarly, applying Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to $A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes
   435	  \Id_\bob \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b}$ and $\{\Id_\alice
   436	  \otimes B^x_{a,c}\}$, and using the fact that $\{B^x_{a,b,c}\}$ is projective,
   437	  we have
   438	  \begin{equation}
   439	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-2}
   440	    \begin{split}
   441	      A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes B^x_{a,\, c}
   442	      & \approx_\delta \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, c} B^x_{a,\, b}\\
   443	      & =_{\phantom{\delta}} \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.
   444	    \end{split}
   445	  \end{equation}
   446	  Combining Equations~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-1}
   447	  and~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-2}, we have
   448	  \begin{equation}
   449	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-3}
   450	    A^x_{a,\, b} C^x_{a,\, c} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\delta
   451	    \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.
   452	  \end{equation}
   453	  A similar argument gives
   454	  \begin{equation}
   455	    \label{eq:commutation-analysis-4}
   456	    C^x_{a,\, c} A^x_{a,\, b} \otimes \Id_\bob \approx_\delta
   457	    \Id_\alice \otimes B^x_{a,\, b,\, c}\,.
   458	  \end{equation}
   459	  The claim follows from Equations~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-3}
   460	  and~\eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-4}.
   461	\end{proof}

   465	The following lemma is a slightly modified version of~\cite[Fact~4.34]{NW19}.
   466	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:ld-sandwich}
   467	  Let $k \geq 0$ be an integer and let $\eps>0$.
   468	  Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution over $\mX$.
   469	  For each $1 \leq i \leq k$ let $\mG_i$ be a finite set of functions $g_i : \mY
   470	  \rightarrow \mR_i$ and for each $x \in \mX$ let $\{G^{i,\, x}_g\}_{g\in
   471	    \mG_i}$ be a projective measurement.
   472	  Suppose that for all $i\in \{1,\ldots,k\}$, $\mG_i$ satisfies the following
   473	  property: for any two $g_i \neq g_i' \in \mG_i$, the probability that $g_i(y)
   474	  = g_i'(y)$ over a uniformly random $y \in \mY$ is at most $\eps$.
   475	
   476	  Let $\bigl\{ A^{x}_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_k} \bigr\}$ be a projective
   477	  measurement with outcomes $(g_1,\ldots,g_k) \in \mG_1\times\cdots\times
   478	  \mG_k$.
   479	  For each $1 \leq i \leq k$, suppose that on average over $x \sim \mu$ and
   480	  $y\in \mY$ sampled uniformly at random,
   481	  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-sandwich-1}
   482	    A^{x}_{[\eval_y(\cdot)_i = a_i]} \abc G^{i,\, x}_{[\eval_y(\cdot)=a_i]}\;.
   483	  \end{equation}
   484	  Define the POVM family $\{C^x_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_k}\}$, for $x\in \mX$, by
   485	  \begin{equation*}
   486	    C^x_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_k} = G^{k,\, x}_{g_1} \cdots
   487	    G^{2,\, x}_{g_{k-1}} \, G^{1,\, x}_{g_k} \, G^{2,\, x}_{g_{k-1}} \cdots
   488	    G^{k,\, x}_{g_1}\;.
   489	  \end{equation*}
   490	  Then on average over $x\sim \mu$ and $y\in \mY$ sampled uniformly at random,
   491	  \begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-sandwich-2}
   492	    A^x_{[\eval_y(\cdot) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots,\, a_k)]} \abc[k(\delta+\eps)^{1/2}]
   493	    C^x_{[\eval_y(\cdot) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots,\, a_k)]}\;.
   494	\end{equation}

/-!
# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project

This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.

## Main definitions

* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.

## References

This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/

/--
A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
-/
structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
  /-- The effect operators. -/
  effect : α → Op d
  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1

/--
A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
-/
structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    extends Submeasurement α d where
  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1

/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/

namespace Submeasurement

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/

/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
  ∑ a, M.effect a

/--
Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
fibers.
-/
noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
  sum_le_one := by
    calc
      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one

/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    M.total ≤ 1 := by
  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one

/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm

/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm

end Submeasurement

namespace Measurement

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

/--
Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.

This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
-/
def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
  effect := effect
  pos := pos
  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one

/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
    M.total = 1 :=
  M.sum_eq_one

/--
Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.

This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
remains a POVM after postprocessing.
-/
noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
  sum_eq_one := by
    calc
      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
  rfl

@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
  rfl

end Measurement

/-! ## Overlap definitions -/

section Overlap

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)

/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)

end Overlap

   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,
   128	  $L_1(x)=0$ for all $x\in V$, and $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is the $0$ map for all
   129	  $x\in V$.
   130	\end{remark}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}
   384

   387	Section~\ref{sec:ldt}).
   388	However, the introspection protocol in Section~\ref{sec:introspection} handles

/-!
# Quantitative state and operator distances

The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
estimates to later proof stages.

## References

These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT
open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/--
Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/
noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    [DecidableEq ι]
    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2

/--
Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/
noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness

The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:180-220`,
from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:181-191`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
      if a = b then 0 else
        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:181-191`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ

/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ

/-- Lean-only unfolding lemma for the unit-alphabet specialization of
`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`, paper
`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl

/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`, with local
identifications induced by explicit type equalities; blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:212-219`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`.
Both operator distances use the source-permitted state vector `S.ψ`. -/
structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
  /-- Explicit equality of Alice's local spaces. -/
  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
  /-- Explicit equality of Bob's local spaces. -/
  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
      S.ψ ≤ δ
  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
      S.ψ ≤ δ

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-! # Strategy classes and symmetric games

This module defines projective, commuting, consistent, PCC, and SPCC strategy
predicates from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:89-169`, with source
definitions in `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-180`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

universe u

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- Projectivity from `def:projective-strategy-general`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:90-101`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`. -/
def Strategy.IsProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.A x)) ∧
    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.B y)

/-- Symmetric games from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:98-107`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
The source equalities of question and answer alphabets are encoded by single
shared carriers, matching its compact notation. -/
structure SymmetricGame where
  Question : Type
  Answer : Type
  [questionFintype : Fintype Question]
  [answerFintype : Fintype Answer]
  [questionDecidableEq : DecidableEq Question]
  [answerDecidableEq : DecidableEq Answer]
  μ : Distribution (Question × Question)
  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
  μ_symm : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x)
  decide : Question → Question → Answer → Answer → Bool
  decide_symm : ∀ x y a b, decide x y a b = decide y x b a

attribute [instance] SymmetricGame.questionFintype SymmetricGame.answerFintype
  SymmetricGame.questionDecidableEq SymmetricGame.answerDecidableEq

/-- Lean-only coercion supporting `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:98-107`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
def SymmetricGame.toGame (G : SymmetricGame) : Game where
  QuestionA := G.Question
  QuestionB := G.Question
  AnswerA := G.Answer
  AnswerB := G.Answer
  μ := G.μ
  μ_prob := G.μ_prob
  decide := G.decide

/-- Symmetric strategies from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:98-107`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
The source equalities of local spaces and measurements are encoded by one
shared local carrier and one measurement family. -/
structure SymmetricStrategy (G : SymmetricGame) where
  ι : Type
  [ιFintype : Fintype ι]
  [ιDecidableEq : DecidableEq ι]
  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)
  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
  ψ_swap : reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) ψ = ψ
  M : G.Question → Measurement G.Answer ι

attribute [instance] SymmetricStrategy.ιFintype SymmetricStrategy.ιDecidableEq

/-- Lean-only coercion supporting `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:98-107`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
def SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy {G : SymmetricGame} (S : SymmetricStrategy G) :
    Strategy G.toGame where
  ιA := S.ι
  ιB := S.ι
  ψ := S.ψ
  ψ_norm := S.ψ_norm
  A := S.M
  B := S.M

/-- Common-space commutation from `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:135-142`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
def IsCommutingOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β]
    [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution (X × Y)) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
    (B : Y → Measurement β ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, 0 < μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((B y).effect b)

private def transportOp {d₁ d₂ : Type u} (h : d₁ = d₂) (M : Op d₂) : Op d₁ :=
  h.symm ▸ M

/-- Transported common-space form of `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:135-142`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
def Strategy.IsCommuting {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (hι : S.ιA = S.ιB) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y, 0 < G.μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b,
    Commute ((S.A x).effect a) (transportOp hι ((S.B y).effect b))

/-- Measurement consistency from `def:consistent-measurement`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:144-157`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:144-160`. -/
def Measurement.IsConsistentOn {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
  ∀ a, (heteroKron (M.effect a) 1).mulVec ψ =
    (heteroKron 1 (M.effect a)).mulVec ψ

/-- General strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:159-162`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
def IsConsistentStrategyOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B : Y → Measurement β ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧
    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (B y) ψ

/-- Symmetric strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:159-162`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
def SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent {G : SymmetricGame}
    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (S.M x) S.ψ

/-- The PCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:166-169`,
paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
def Strategy.IsPCC {G : Game} {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution (G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB))
    (A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ι)
    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ι)
  (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x)) ∧
    (∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (B y)) ∧
    IsConsistentStrategyOn A B ψ ∧ IsCommutingOn μ A B

/-- The SPCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:166-169`,
paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
def SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC {G : SymmetricGame}
  (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.M x)) ∧ S.IsConsistent ∧
    IsCommutingOn G.μ S.M S.M

/-- Source symmetrization statement `lem:symmetric-strat`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:112-132`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
The attainment defect is `rem:symmetric-strat-limit` and is tracked in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy (G : SymmetricGame) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : G.toGame.value = 1 - ε) :
    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
      1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
  sorry

/-- Lean-only given-strategy form associated with `lem:symmetric-strat`, blueprint
`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:112-132`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
The source attainment distinction is tracked in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_of_strategy (G : SymmetricGame)
    (ε : ℝ) (S₀ : Strategy G.toGame) (h : 1 - ε ≤ S₀.value) :
    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
      1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
  sorry

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
